Retired Classroom Attendance Competitor has shut down — here's your migration path

If you relied on a legacy Classroom attendance competitor add-on, its Google Workspace Marketplace listing confirmed that the add-on was retired on March 1, 2026 and has stopped functioning. If you need a reliable, actively maintained replacement for your classes, here is what to do, in order.

The short version: convert any past attendance CSV files you saved, pick Attendance Tracker as your actively maintained replacement built on official Google APIs, and re-import your Google Classroom rosters in one click. The whole switch takes about five minutes.
What happened

The retired competitor's Marketplace listing announced that the add-on was retired and ceased functioning on March 1, 2026. This wasn't a rumor — it was the developer's published notice. The tool no longer records attendance for Google Meet sessions.

Retirements like this are common in this category. Two other attendance competitor tools have died recently: one Chrome extension competitor was delisted from the Chrome Web Store in September 2025, and another legacy extension competitor has been unmaintained since 2021 and no longer works with modern Chrome. When a free tool's developer moves on, the tool goes with them — which is why maintenance cadence should be near the top of your checklist when you pick a replacement.
Migrating your data and rosters
There is no automatic direct transfer between attendance tools — each stores records in its own format. Here is how to handle your records and classes:

Check past exports or Google Drive. If you downloaded past CSVs or if the tool ever wrote attendance to Sheets in your Drive, those files are yours. You can use our interactive roster converter below to bring those student lists into Attendance Tracker.

Google Classroom rosters are safe. Your Google Classroom rosters live in Classroom itself, not in the old attendance tool — they are completely safe and will re-import into Attendance Tracker in one click.
Start your next class seamlessly. Once your rosters are connected, Attendance Tracker handles live tracking, auto-sorting, and Sheets exports without any disruption to your semester.

What to look for in a replacement
Actively maintained. The single biggest lesson from this shutdown. Look for a tool with recent, frequent updates — not one last touched years ago.

An official add-on, not a screen scraper. Chrome extensions that scrape the Meet participant list break whenever Google updates Meet's UI, and they can't run on Firefox, Safari, or managed school Chromebooks. An official Meet add-on runs in the Activities panel and reads attendance from the official Google Meet REST API.
Google Classroom roster support. If your class lists live in Classroom, the replacement should import them directly instead of making you retype names.
Exports you can keep. CSV, Sheets, or gradebook-format exports mean your records are never trapped in one tool again.

All of the above is on the free tier. Because it's an add-on rather than a browser extension, there's nothing to install per-device, and a Meet UI redesign can't break it.
The 3-step switch
Step 1: Install
Install Attendance Tracker from the Google Workspace Marketplace (button below). It appears in Google Meet under the Activities panel — no extension, no per-student setup.
Step 2: Import your Classroom roster
In the side panel, open Class Roster → + New Class → Import from Google Classroom. Pick your class and the full student list imports in one click. Repeat for each class you teach.
Step 3: Track your next class

Join your next Meet, open Attendance Tracker, and press Start. Students are matched to the roster automatically and sorted into Present, Late, and Absent in real time. Export or review history whenever you need it.
Why maintenance cadence matters here

A major Classroom attendance add-on retiring in 2026, another extension competitor delisted in 2025, and another abandoned since 2021 — three competitor tools in one small category, all gone or going. A tool that isn't shipping updates isn't just missing features; it's on borrowed time. Attendance Tracker is actively maintained, with multiple updates shipping weekly through 2026, and it's available in 60 languages.
Frequently asked questions
Will my old attendance data transfer automatically?

No — there's no automatic direct transfer between attendance tools. If you saved past CSV exports from a previous attendance competitor, you can use our free browser-based roster migration tool above to convert them into an Attendance Tracker roster. Your Google Classroom rosters themselves are unaffected and re-import into Attendance Tracker in one click.
Is Attendance Tracker free?

Yes. The free tier includes the real-time roster, Class Rosters with Classroom import, CSV/Excel downloads, gradebook CSVs, PDF reports, and the Meeting History dashboard. Pro adds extras like hands-free auto-capture and unlimited Sheets exports.
